title: Cross-Corridor Conversion: From Authorization To Operation
summary: Compare how Northern Virginia compute, Nevada lithium, and Florida Space Coast infrastructure move from demand, permits, financing, and plans into construction, acceptance, service, operation, and measured outcomes.
current_state_summary: All three corridors now have deeper implementation dossiers; Florida closes two physical or operating stages, while Northern Virginia service and Nevada qualified output remain unproven.
current_state: Northern Virginia has load, rate, transmission, permit, and water rails; final route, construction, energization, customer service, use, and reliability remain incomplete.

Nevada has federal land decisions, state permits, and a closed Thacker Pass loan; condition satisfaction, construction, commissioning, qualification, output, sales, and environmental performance remain incomplete.

Florida has master plans, site licensing, environmental decisions, operator rules, and capital channels; named project funding, construction, acceptance, mission authorization, utilization, and outcomes remain incomplete.
Florida now has an operational access bridge and one completed active-countdown resilience operation, but mission licensing and measured system outcomes remain incomplete.
Research Watches 001 and 002 and Local Authorization Is Not Operation expose the shared stage-conversion problem without treating the corridors as legally or technically equivalent.

dependency_stack.current_state: Each corridor has named upstream records that establish demand, rules, plans, permits, environmental decisions, or financing stages.
dependency_stack.boundary: The instruments differ and none alone proves a completed, accepted, operating, or scaled asset.

dependency_stack.current_state: Named projects have partial construction, permitting, route, finance, environmental, inspection, assurance, testing, and service trails; Kennedy's causeway bridge closes one physical delivery stage.
dependency_stack.boundary: Partial trails do not establish that all conditions were satisfied, assets were built and accepted, or compliance was sustained.

dependency_stack.current_state: The next decisive records differ by corridor: customer service, qualified material output, or authorized mission use.
dependency_stack.boundary: Projected demand, output, or launch cadence cannot stand in for delivered service, accepted products, or completed missions.

dependency_stack.current_state: One Kennedy operating adaptation is documented, but no corridor record set supports a complete claim about sustained capacity, cost, reliability, safety, environmental performance, or local outcomes.
dependency_stack.boundary: Scale requires sustained operating evidence and measured receiving-system results.

evidence_limits: The pathway compares evidence stages, not economic, environmental, institutional, or technical equivalence.
A rate decision, mining permit, federal loan, site license, environmental decision, and master plan are not interchangeable.
No pathway record establishes corridor-wide readiness, spare capacity, qualified output, mission availability, or accepted local outcomes.
next_records: Northern Virginia route, construction, energization, customer-service, water, emissions-compliance, reliability, and local-outcome records.
Nevada finance draws, water and permit-condition compliance, construction, commissioning, qualification, output, sales, environmental, and repayment records.
Florida project appropriations, awards, construction, acceptance, operator and mission authorization, utilization, safety, resilience, and outcome records.
